statement: Suppose that the data of Proposition 2.2 exist, with m ≥ 5, p ≥ 9 extra letters, and the finite family of independently conjugated boundary laws described there. Their Brunnian property means that omitting any slot makes the law the identity, as in Equation (2.1). There are a characteristic-zero field K, internal coordinate blocks hi for the 2m edges, and algebraic power-series germs Fi(hi) and bi(hi), the latter for the m active edges, with the following properties. Put T = K[ti : i active]/(t2 i : i active), S0 = ∑ i Fi, St = S0 + ∑ i active tibi. There are formal parametrizations HL(x, t) over T and HR(y) over K whose central tangent maps are injective and have complementary images in the full internal coordinate space. They are smooth graph germs over T and K, respectively, and St(HL) = 0, S0(HR) = 0. (6.1) For every three distinct active indices i, j, k, titjtk ∈ ((∂ha St)(HL) : a = 1, . . . , N) ⊂ T[[x]], (6.2) (bibjbk)(HR) ∈ ((∂ha S0)(HR) : a = 1, . . . , N) ⊂ K[[y]], (6.3) where N is the total number of internal coordinates. The field can be taken to be K = C((σ)). The individual functions can be normalized so that Fi(0) = bi(0) = 0.
